newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector flies to southeast Asia -- TV.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector flies to southeast Asia -- TV.

text.p: North Korea's top ideologue left Beijing on Tuesday nearly five weeks after seeking asylum in a South Korean diplomatic mission, Yonhap Television News quoted a government source in Seoul as saying.
The source said Hwang Jang-yop headed for a southeast Asian country but gave no other details.
A foreign ministry spokesman declined comment on the report. He said China and South Korea would announce Hwang's departure after he had landed in a third country.

Airport officials in Xiamen, China, meanwhile, said a special flight left Beijing's Xiyuan airport for the southeastern coastal city of Xiamen carrying a passenger who would take a connecting flight to Manila.
The Chinese officials said they were unable to identify the passenger.
Hwang, the most senior North Korean official to flee the troubled communist state, has been stranded in the South Korean consulate since arriving there with an aide on February 12.

Beijing has been trying to find a solution to the problem of how to hand over Hwang to new business partner Seoul while appearing to give consideration to the concerns of old communist ally Pyongyang.
South Korea's influential Chosun Ilbo newspaper said Hwang and his aide slipped out of South Korea's consulate overnight.
The domestic media have said the Philippines was the most likely first stop.
On Monday a senior South Korean official said Hwang would stay in a third country "for a considerable period of time" before coming to South Korea.
He said the Philippines was one of several "transit points" being considered.
Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said on Saturday his country had been asked to serve as a transit point for Hwang if he were allowed to leave for South Korea.
A top Manila Foreign Office official said Hwang would very likely stay in the Philippines for a few days, but added that it was possible his country was being used as a decoy.

Hwang, ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy, is credited with devising the national creed of "juche", which stresses self-reliance and has kept North Korea frozen in Stalinist-era isolation and economic backwardness.
